intro.title: Collaborate with MARVI
intro.lede: MARVI works with communities, governments, NGOs, researchers and educators interested in practical approaches to groundwater stewardship.

blocks.title: Use the MARVI approach

items.title: Bhujal Jankaars
items.text: “Groundwater informed”: local volunteers who connect careful observation with community knowledge and collective action.

items.title: OurWater app
items.text: A free, community-focused water monitoring and learning app, built on the MARVI approach.

blocks.title: Research collaboration
blocks.lede: The project works across hydrology, hydrogeology, agronomy, economics and social science. The result is not a report left on a shelf, but knowledge a community can use.

items.title: People & Partners
items.text: Researchers, practitioners and village volunteers in India and Australia working as one team.

items.title: Publications
items.text: Brochures and books from the project — free to download in English, Hindi and Gujarati. Grouped by kind; filter or search to narrow the list.

blocks.title: Training & capacity building
blocks.lede: These trained volunteers measure wells, rainfall, water quality and check dams. They interpret local patterns, explain them in the community’s own language and help farmers see that groundwater is both limited and shared.

items.title: Learn about groundwater
items.text: Rain moves through soil and rock into an aquifer. Wells reveal only a small window into a connected underground system.

items.title: Groundwater game
items.text: A whole village draws from one aquifer. Every crop and every turn reveals why groundwater decisions cannot be made alone.

items.title: Videos
items.text: A curated starting point from the new MARVI video archive—introductions, field stories, training and technical talks.
